mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 12 months prior to the rate hike (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month rolling window, the correlation between PAYEMS acceleration and SPX 20-day returns is < 0.2 (Spearman's rho).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,400K for four consecutive months indicates renewed builder confidence and expanding credit availability, which accelerates equity market valuation growth and drives positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST remains above 1,400K for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 30 such monthly spikes, the average 5-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly convergence of industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer goods production (not available in catalog) toward historical averages above 102 suggests a supply-side easing that reduces production bottlenecks, resulting in positive 20-day S&P 500 returns when triggered by a falling CPIAUCSL.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 102 while CPIAUCSL decreases by > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: In regimes where CPIAUCSL declines are not accompanied by SPX outperformance (20-day returns flat or negative).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% for two consecutive months triggers the Fed to maintain a higher terminal rate, which raises the discount rate applied to equities and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns remain positive despite CPIAUCSL > 3% for the subsequent 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% without a corresponding rise in labor turnover (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market that reduces wage growth, which in turn dampens equity risk premia and yields negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% for 6 consecutive months while PAYEMS does not increase by > 5% month-over-month
failure_condition: Over a 2-year window, the average 60-day return during tight labor markets is not significantly different from a neutral (zero) return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained multi-month convergence of all major macro proxies (GDPC1 demand, RSAFS demand, INDPRO supply, HOUST demand) toward their long-run means creates a regime of macroeconomic balance that is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In equilibrium regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than during periods of macro imbalance (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time cut in the federal funds rate by 0.25% at the end of the previous month, observed as a spike in FEDFUNDS, produces a short-lived liquidity boost that drives positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS shows a one-time monthly drop of > 0.25% after a steady increase for the prior 3 months
failure_condition: The 5-day return is not significantly different from zero when controlling for pre-cut market volatility (F-test p > 0.05).
